author_reading.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
author_reading.rationale: A registered Gray pointer is sampled directly as a three-bit bus in clk_b with no synchronizer stages; the source and destination use separately timed synchronous reset inputs.

rationale: Registered Gray data is captured in only one clk_b stage, whose state is directly exposed. Gray encoding does not contain metastability. The separate clk_a-related rst_b_n reset crossing does not remove this designated short-chain defect.

labels.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
labels.rationale: Registered Gray coding does not replace metastability containment: wgray has only one clk_b capture stage and that stage is directly exposed as wseen. Additionally rst_b_n is explicitly clk_a-launched and directly controls clk_b capture. Reset coordination and bit-skew proof are absent, but neither removes the short-chain defect. Unfit for an isolated single-defect Gray test because reset adds a separate concrete crossing.

labels.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
labels.rationale: The registered Gray counter has only one destination capture stage, exposed directly as wseen. Gray coding does not contain metastability without a destination synchronization chain. Independently, rst_b_n is constrained to clk_a and used as a synchronous clk_b reset; that additional defect does not change the Gray-chain verdict. UNFIT for isolation of a single defect.
